Reinforcement Learning Trees

Source: R/RLT.r
RLT.Rd

Fit random forest models for regression, classification and survival analysis. By default, splits use one variable at a time. Set reinforcement = TRUE to use embedded-model guidance for single-variable splits, or linear.comb > 1 for linear combination splits. Linear combination splits do not require reinforcement = TRUE; regression and classification combination splits still use embedded screening at sufficiently large nodes. See param.control for details.

Usage

RLT(
  x,
  y,
  censor = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  ntrees = if (reinforcement) 100 else 500,
  mtry = max(1, as.integer(ncol(x)/2)),
  nmin = 5,
  alpha = 0,
  nsplit = 0,
  resample.replace = TRUE,
  resample.prob = if (resample.replace) 1 else 0.8,
  resample.preset = NULL,
  obs.w = NULL,
  var.prob = NULL,
  importance = FALSE,
  reinforcement = FALSE,
  linear.comb = 1,
  linear.comb.method = "default",
  split.rule = "default",
  var.mode = "none",
  param.control = list(),
  ncores = 0,
  verbose = 0,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or a data.frame of features. Unordered factors in a data frame use categorical splits. Ordered factors and character columns retain their numerical rank-code treatment. Training label dictionaries are saved for all three types, so prediction and kernels match labels to the training codes. Numeric inputs for these columns are interpreted as integer training codes in 1:length(training_labels), not as labels. Character matrices are not supported.

y

Response vector: numeric for regression or observed survival times, and a factor for classification.

censor

Survival event indicator: 1 for an observed event and 0 for a right-censored observation.

model

The model type: "regression", "classification", or "survival". Quantile forest is not yet implemented.

ntrees

Number of trees, ntrees = 100 if reinforcement is used and ntrees = 500 otherwise.

mtry

Number of randomly selected variables used at each internal node. Default: max(1, floor(p/2)).

nmin

Terminal node size. Splitting will stop when the internal node size is less equal to nmin. Default: 5.

alpha

Minimum proportion of samples (of the parent node) enforced in each child node. Default: 0 (no constraint). Clamped to the range 0 to 0.5.

nsplit

Number of random cutting points to compare for each variable at an internal node. Default: 0 (use all unique values, i.e., best split). When nsplit > 0, random cutting points are generated.

resample.replace

Whether the in-bag samples are obtained with replacement.

resample.prob

Proportion of in-bag samples.

resample.preset

A pre-specified matrix for in-bag data indicator/count matrix. It must be an \(n \times\) ntrees matrix with integer entries. Positive number indicates the number of copies of that observation (row) in the corresponding tree (column); zero indicates out-of-bag; negative values indicates not being used in either. Extremely large counts should be avoided. The sum of each column should not exceed \(n\).

obs.w

Observation weights. The weights will be used for calculating the splitting scores, such as a weighted variance reduction or weighted gini index. But they will not be used for sampling observations. In that case, one can pre-specify resample.preset instead for balanced sampling, etc. For survival analysis, observation weights are supported in the "logrank", "suplogrank", and "coxgrad" splitting rules. Weighted logrank and suplogrank use a variance estimator that accounts for the observation weights. Weights must be finite and nonnegative with positive total mass; individual zero weights are allowed. A sampled outer or embedded tree with zero total observation weight produces a catchable error.

var.prob

Variable probabilities for split variable selection. A numeric vector of length p (number of predictors) with finite nonnegative weights and positive total mass. The vector is normalized internally and guides sampling of split candidates. In particular, requesting the whole candidate pool returns all variables, and some regression/classification linear combination screening paths sample uniformly. Zero-probability exclusion is therefore not guaranteed across these paths. If NULL (default), uniform sampling is used.

importance

Whether to calculate variable importance. Use TRUE or "permute" to measure the deterioration in out-of-bag (OOB) performance after permuting a predictor. With "distribute", an OOB observation follows both children whenever a split uses the assessed predictor. Routing probabilities are proportional to child node weights, or sample counts for unweighted data. Regression and classification average terminal-node losses; survival evaluates concordance using averaged terminal-node risk scores. Both strategies are available for regression, classification, and survival. Survival importance uses OOB concordance and is unavailable when no usable OOB comparisons exist.

reinforcement

Whether to use embedded-model guidance for single-variable splits. Default: FALSE. Linear combination splits are selected separately by linear.comb; see param.control for their model-specific screening behavior.

linear.comb

Maximum number of variables in each linear combination split. Default: 1 (single-variable splits). Values greater than 1 do not require reinforcement = TRUE. See linear.comb.method and param.control.

linear.comb.method

Method for constructing linear combinations. "default" selects "sir" for regression, "lda" for classification, and "coxph" for survival. See param.control for all methods.

split.rule

Splitting criterion. Default "default" selects the standard rule for each model. For survival: "logrank", "suplogrank", or "coxgrad". See param.control.

var.mode

Variance estimation mode: "none" (default), "matched", "IJ", or "jack". TRUE is equivalent to "matched". Matched sampling supports prediction and importance variance; IJ and jackknife modes support prediction variance. Active modes adjust resampling settings and retain observation tracking. See param.control.

param.control

A list of additional forest and embedded-model settings. Reinforcement is available for regression, classification, and survival. Embedded-model defaults are provided automatically but may need tuning.

Embedded-model settings:

  • embed.ntrees: number of embedded trees. Default: 50.

  • embed.mtry: candidate-variable proportion when less than 1, or count when at least 1. Default: 0.5.

  • embed.nmin: embedded terminal node size. Default: 5.

  • embed.nsplit: random cutting points; 0 uses the best split. Default: 3.

  • embed.resample.replace: sample with replacement. Default: TRUE.

  • embed.resample.prob: sample proportion within the current node. Default: 0.9.

  • embed.mute: variables to mute per split, as a count when at least 1 or a proportion when less than 1. Default: 0 (no muting).

  • embed.protect: number of top variables protected from muting. Default: ceiling(log(n)).

  • embed.threshold: threshold relative to the best importance for inclusion in the protected set. Default: 0.25.

Linear combination settings:

  • linear.comb: maximum variables per combination. Default: 1. Values greater than 1 select combination splits independently of reinforcement. Regression and classification use embedded importance screening when the node has at least 3 * embed.nmin observations and direct screening at smaller nodes. Survival combination splits screen mtry candidates without an embedded forest.

  • linear.comb.method: regression accepts "naive", "lm", "pca", and "sir" (default); classification accepts "lda" (default), "naive", "random", and "logistic"; survival accepts "coxph" (default) and "naive".

split.rule selects the splitting criterion:

  • Regression: "var" (variance reduction).

  • Classification: "gini" (Gini index).

  • Survival: "logrank" (default), "suplogrank", or "coxgrad".

resample.track retains the in-bag count for each observation and tree. Default: FALSE. All active variance modes enable it automatically.

var.mode prepares variance estimation during fitting:

  • "none" (default): no variance estimation.

  • "matched" (or TRUE): matched-sample U-statistic decomposition for prediction and variable importance variance. Uses paired half-samples without replacement, sets resample.prob = 0.5, and generates resample.preset, replacing any supplied preset. An odd ntrees is reduced to the preceding even number; at least 2 are required.

  • "IJ": infinitesimal jackknife prediction variance.

  • "jack": jackknife-after-bootstrap prediction variance.

IJ and jackknife modes set resample.replace = TRUE, retain the requested resample.prob, and generate bootstrap counts instead of using a supplied resample.preset. They do not estimate variable importance variance. All active variance modes enable importance = "distribute" when importance was disabled; an explicitly requested importance method is retained. Stable variance estimates generally require many trees. IJ and jackknife modes recommend at least 2000 trees.

time.grid.size is 0 by default and retains all distinct observed failure times for survival fitting. A positive integer must be at least the number of distinct failure times; it does not add times to the training grid. Requests that would reduce the training grid are rejected. Use band.grid.size in predict() to reduce the evaluation grid instead.

ncores

Number of CPU logical cores. Default is 0 (using all available cores when compiled with OpenMP). Builds without OpenMP run serially.

verbose

Whether info should be printed.

seed

Random seed number to replicate a previously fitted forest. Internally, the xoshiro256++ generator is used. If not specified, a seed will be generated automatically and recorded.

...

Additional arguments.

Value

A fitted object of class RLT. OOB predictions for each training observation use only trees that did not sample that observation.

Prediction

OOB numeric predictions for regression, factor labels for classification, or a matrix of hazard increments for survival. Survival rows correspond to observations and columns to timepoints.

Error

OOB mean squared error for regression, misclassification rate for classification, or \(1-C\) for survival. The survival concordance score uses the sum of the OOB cumulative hazards over the failure-time grid, not just the cumulative hazard at the final time. Lower error is better.

VarImp

Variable importance when requested. Use importance to obtain a named summary.

FittedForest

Fitted tree structures.

xlevels

Training label dictionaries for factor, ordered-factor, and character data-frame columns, with NULL entries for numerical features.

ObsTrack

Provided if resample.track = TRUE, var.mode != "none", or if resample.preset was supplied. This is an n \(\times\) ntrees matrix that has the same meaning as resample.preset.

Classification forests also provide:

nclass

Number of response classes.

Prob

OOB class probabilities, with one row per observation and one column per class in the order given by ylabels.

Survival forests also provide:

timepoints

ordered observed failure times

NFail

The number of observed failure times

References

  • Zhu, R., Zeng, D., & Kosorok, M. R. (2015) "Reinforcement Learning Trees." Journal of the American Statistical Association. 110(512), 1770-1784.

  • Xu, T., Zhu, R., & Shao, X. (2023) "On Variance Estimation of Random Forests with Infinite-Order U-statistics." arXiv preprint arXiv:2202.09008.

  • Formentini, S. E., Wei L., & Zhu, R. (2022) "Confidence Band Estimation for Survival Random Forests." arXiv preprint arXiv:2204.12038.

Examples

# \donttest{
  set.seed(42)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 5), ncol = 5)
  y <- rowSums(x[, 1:2]) + rnorm(300)
  fit <- RLT(x, y, ntrees = 100)
  print(fit)
#> -----------------------------------------
#> RLT Regression Forest
#> -----------------------------------------
#>               (N, P) = (300, 5)
#>           # of trees = 100
#>         (mtry, nmin) = (2, 5)
#>       split generate = Best
#>             sampling = 100% w/ replace
#>           importance = none
#>             OOB MSE = 1.385 (R2 = 0.5361)
#> -----------------------------------------
# }
